An illustration of the \emph{shifted window} approach for computing self-attention in the proposed Swin Transformer architecture. In layer $l$ (left), a regular window partitioning scheme is adopted, and self-attention is computed within each window. 
    In the next layer $l+1$ (right), the window partitioning is shifted, resulting in new windows. The self-attention computation in the new windows crosses the boundaries of the previous windows in layer $l$, providing connections among them.
